investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: retained evidence acquired via curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion) with a descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser. A plain curl GET of the public homepage immediately exposed 4 <script type="application/ld+json"> Event blocks. One had a malformed JSON body (a real-world producer imperfection); this package's json-ld/parse.mjs skips a malformed block rather than aborting the others, and 3 valid records were retained.

identity.notes: Official identity confirmed directly from the retained evidence at https://www.harlemjazzclub.es/.

site_classification.platform: WordPress; the homepage embeds one schema.org Event JSON-LD block per upcoming show.

title.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'name' field (this source embeds the show time and price directly in the name text, e.g. '10:30 PM | MR SHINGLES...').

start_date.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'startDate' — a non-standard but unambiguous shape ('2026-8-27T22:30+2:00': non-zero-padded month/hour/offset, no seconds); this package's collector (ingestion/json-ld/observation-adapter.mjs) reconstructs the equivalent strictly-padded ISO string mechanically before parsing, never guessing a value.

end.notes: Each JSON-LD Event's own 'endDate', same non-standard-but-unambiguous shape.

source_record_id.notes: No numeric id or location field is exposed at all; each event's own 'url' field is this source's own permanent '/events/{slug}/...' page, so the slug is used as source_record_id.

reasons: A CONFIRMED public data path retained.
title and start_date both PROVEN (start_date via a documented, mechanical, non-guessing offset-padding reconstruction).
source_record_id PROVEN via a documented URL-slug strategy.
